title: “Joe would have liked to see Ari out strolling on Sunday!” #westend #...
transcript: When Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey were first announced to be in Sunday in the park with George, I made a video sort of implying that it might be better if it didn't end up happening. And now this is awkward. The point I was making is that there is maybe such a thing as a theater production that generates so much demand that it becomes a genuine strain on the infrastructure of theater. And I sort of compared it to the Infinity Gauntlet or the One Ring, something that might just be too powerful to continue existing. So am I happy now that both of the stars have dropped out of the production? No, of course I'm not happy, especially because of the sensitive circumstances around Ariana Grande's departure. And Sunday in the park with George is my favorite musical of all time. And I know they say that the production has not been cancelled. It's gonna go on ahead. But, you know, that may or may not turn out to be true. And that would be a shame for a number of reasons. But the biggest one for me is that Marianne Elliot, I think, is one of the smartest and most skilled directors working today. And not only that, but something I've always said she's particularly skilled at is using visuals and spectacle in a way that feels fully integrated into the storytelling. And this is literally a show about visual art. So I think it would be a real shame if she doesn't get a crack at this. Having said that, I would be lying if I denied feeling a small twinge of relief that I don't have to deal with the anxiety of getting tickets to this and getting myself over to London at the right time. Like, I genuinely would have lost sleep over this. And is that a sign that I have a problem? Absolutely. But the point stands. Yes, I would have loved to have seen this in real life. But maybe, just maybe, Ariana Grande's dot is better off as this fantastical idea for all of us to share in our collective imagination.
